fpu.protocol: the EXISTING caller-environment guard of model_step.c (enter_environment/leave_environment): requires the original exception masks (x87 63, SSE 63), saves the caller COMPLETE state (fegetenv + MXCSR), sets round-toward-zero for both units, runs the statements in a noinline body, restores the caller state and reads it back. No new mechanism, no global normalisation.
fpu.original_characterised: tests/csrc/city_box_control.c holds the ORIGINAL statements and the two maths routines verbatim (the test the_controls_statements_are_the_originals compares them with ct_msgs.c and matrix.c on every run, and the host copy in eech_arith.h by squeezed text). Measured on Linux/glibc over 9 headings: the original statements leave the x87 control word and the MXCSR control and mask bits untouched, run under RTZ with all masks set, and raise only the sticky inexact flag (MXCSR 0x20); nothing in aphavoc/modules reads a status flag and the engine entry restores the caller state, so the flag is unobservable.
fpu.difference_recorded: the host kernel restores the caller state INCLUDING status flags, so the original sticky inexact flag is not carried; it is unobservable (no reader, engine entry restores)
fpu.boot_caller: the callback is entered under the engine RTZ; the same guard already serves the boot-time TARGET_POINT_OFFSET/scene-bounds kernels, so no legitimate boot is newly rejected; native confirmation of masks 63 at this call is Root's actual
fpu.tests: the kernel equals the control bit for bit over 4 scenes x 9 headings x 5 offsets x 4 boxes x 2 caller rounding modes (1440 cases, incl. signed zeros and the empty slot); the caller state (x87 control, MXCSR with sticky flags, all four rounding modes) is returned bit for bit; an unmasked caller exception is refused with state untouched; non-finite words are refused by bits before arithmetic
fpu.unverified: Windows/mingw libm sin/cos behaviour of the original vs the host kernel is Root's native comparison; the Linux control cannot say
